text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- Large-scale operation of police in Tirana cafes and bars after two bomb attacks injured 27 people on Monday and several bomb-threat calls.
- An editorial says that any visit by Italian politicians to Albania prompts a reaction from Athens, which is also trying to strengthen its influence in Albania.
- A European Parliament mission to Albania said political parties should agree they will not contest the outcome of parliamentary elections.
- Gunmen prevented King Leka from visiting the southern town of Saranda where he planned to seek support for the restoration of the monarchy.
ALBANIA
- The paper director said he would sue Interior Ministry state secretary Lush Perpali.
- President Sali Berisha told a European Parliament delegation that he would guarantee free, fair and democratic elections.
- Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos said, during his one-day visit to Albania, that any attempt to boycott elections would be an act of collective suicide.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- A strong explosion destroyed the Democratic Party office in the central town of Elbasan.
- Albanian voters will have their hands stamped just like in Bosnia to avoid possible fraud during elections.
- Police are entitled to open fire without warning against criminals.
- Two young men were maltreated and then burned alive in the southern town of Berat.
INDIPENDENT
- Schools in Tirana were closed after explosions in the capital.
- Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano will stand as candidate in Tepelene town.
- More than 2,000 people gathered at the northwestern beach of Shengjin after rumours that a ship would take them across to Italy.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- The Democratic Party is for a free vote and peace while the Socialists resort to bombs and violence, the paper alleges.
- Europe wants the so-called committees of public salvation to be disbanded before elections.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- President Sali Berisha and his clan are trying to convert Albania into a burning ground.
- Parliament speaker Pjeter Arbnori has refused to convene parliament to lift the state of emergency.
